title: Plurals: les, new verbs, liaison
summary: New verbs entering French become -er verbs: googler, zapper. Plurals add a silent s, so porte and portes sound the same. You hear the plural in les (the / them). Liaison links the s to a following vowel: les amis ('lay-zami').
points: Three verb endings: -er (most common, and all new verbs), -ir (finir, voir), -re (attendre).
Inversion (Puis-je…?) is formal. With friends just say Je peux… ?
Plural nouns add a silent s: la porte → les portes, l'ami → les amis.
les = the (plural) and them, for both genders.
Check the gender when using 'it': la for feminine things (Je la veux), le for masculine.
Liaison: a silent final consonant links to a following vowel when the words belong together: les amis, mon ami.
drills: My friend can wait for you.
